newsitem.title: USA: Broad support for U.S. child food aid - charity.
newsitem.headline: Broad support for U.S. child food aid - charity.

text.p: Child poverty is more widespread in the United States than in other industrialised nations but a charity said on Wednesday there should be broad support in Congress next year to attack childhood hunger.
The charity, Bread for the World, said 500 congressional candidates out of 1,229 contacted had signed a pledge to support federal programmes to help end childhood hunger, if elected.
Spokeswoman Katherine Smith said the results showed "absolutely" that there was broad support for the programmes.

A report prepared by a companion group, Bread for the World Institute, said 21.5 percent of U.S. children were poor, the highest poverty rate among industrialised nations. It said 13.6 million children in the United States were hungry or at risk of hunger.
The report pointed to estimates that the new welfare bill would push an additional 1.1 million children into poverty.
"In the richest nation in the world, it's senseless to have widespread hunger among children," said David Beckman, president of Bread for the World.
